clue.text: Drug in the morning injected into poor Cleopatra

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so one piece is put within the other word's letters
a poor specimen is in bad shape, so the name's letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the hours before noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slips a medicine into the Egyptian queen's veins at dawn, perhaps a modern take on her death.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters for the morning go into the queen's name and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracetamol is a common painkilling medicine, known as acetaminophen in North America, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Noted player, thespian is treading boards

indicators.note: to board is to take on board or hold, so the phrase before it carries the answer inside

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An actor treading the boards on stage is also a musician of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treading the boards' is an idiom for acting, which hides that 'boards' is the signal; 'Noted' is a pun on musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist plays music from written notes on a keyboard instrument, so is a player of noted music.

clue.text: Lad wearing mask investigating after being robbed of PG Tips

indicators.note: something robbed loses part of itself, so letters are taken away from the word

blocks.note: probing a matter is investigating it
the letters P and G are removed; PG Tips is a popular British brand of tea

explanation.surface: A masked boy goes sleuthing after someone has stolen his tea bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman's young sidekick wears a mask. PG Tips is a leading British tea brand, but here the clue only needs its two capital letters taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin, the Boy Wonder of the Batman comics, is a young male companion who hides his face behind a domino mask.

clue.text: Short article about origin of Italian shroud

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its first letter is kept
about means around, so one piece wraps itself round another

blocks.note: a curt reply is a short one
the indefinite article
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brief piece of writing about the beginnings of the Turin Shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' here is the grammar word, not a piece of writing, and 'about' wraps it round the Italian's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain screens or veils something from view, which is the sense of shroud as a covering that conceals.

clue.text: Ingredient for jam-making?

blocks.note: surface reading: something such as fruit or sugar used in making preserves
setter's reading: the jam is a queue of vehicles on a road, built from cars and lorries

explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture of fruit and sugar is the decoy; the jam meant is the one on a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam is made of road vehicles, so the moving cars and lorries are what the hold-up is made from.

clue.text: It puts down roots in road surface, northbound A1

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters go in reverse order

blocks.note: macadam is a road surface of compacted broken stone
the letter A and the digit 1 read as I; A1 is also a major British road

explanation.surface: Something is rooting itself into the tarmac of the A1 heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, which feeds the road picture, but it simply supplies A and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The macadamia is an Australian nut tree, and like any tree it establishes itself by growing roots into the ground.

clue.text: Merry Widow composer necking first of vintage European port

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone
to neck is to swallow, so the composer's name takes something down inside it

blocks.note: Franz Lehár wrote the operetta The Merry Widow
first letter of the word
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The operetta composer knocks back a fine wine, then some continental port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Necking' is slang for drinking down; with vintage and port it makes a wine picture, but port is the harbour sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major seaport on the Normandy coast of northern France, at the mouth of the Seine.

clue.text: One accommodating round room?

blocks.note: first meaning: the part of a gun that holds a cartridge
second meaning: a room, especially a private or formal one

explanation.surface: Some kind of circular room that can house a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a shape for the room; it is a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm's chamber holds the cartridge before firing, and the word is also an old or formal term for a room.

clue.text: Outbreak of awful E. coli beginning to ruin veg

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter only
an outbreak bursts things apart, so these letters break out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nasty food-poisoning outbreak starts to spoil the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak' reads as a bacterial epidemic, which hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauliflower is a brassica with a white edible head, a familiar vegetable; veg is the informal short form.

clue.text: Everyone welcoming company leaders in head office providing booze

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so only the first letters of the following words count
to welcome someone is to take them in, so the word for everyone holds the rest

blocks.note: everyone means all
standard abbreviation
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: All staff welcome company bosses at headquarters, who lay on the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company leaders' looks like one phrase for bosses, but 'company' gives its own abbreviation and 'leaders in' works only on the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink, and alcohol is the general word for such drink.

clue.text: Daily Mail newspaper feature?

blocks.note: surface reading: some regular item in the British tabloid paper called the Daily Mail
setter's reading: the post that arrives each day, which a paper prints as readers' correspondence

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it the name of a tabloid; read as plain words it is the day's post sent in by readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's correspondence section prints the messages readers send in, the mail it receives every day.

clue.text: Number one character from Greece rejected marriage

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read from the other end

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The top-ranked person from Greece turned down a marriage proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a single phrase meaning the best, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two people in wedlock, so it is a formal word for a marriage.

clue.text: Breaking, ITV: FIFA concealing US lawyer’s testimony

indicators.note: something breaking falls apart, so the letters of the two names are scattered
to conceal is to hide inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round the lawyer

blocks.note: taken as written; ITV is a British TV network
taken as written; FIFA runs world football
a district attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Breaking news on a TV channel: football's governing body is hiding a US attorney's evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' sounds like breaking news; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement sworn on oath for use as evidence in court, a form of testimony.

clue.text: Finn discovered his creator split

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: Huckleberry Finn is found within the works of Mark Twain, who wrote him
second meaning: broken into two parts

explanation.surface: A fictional boy finds out who wrote him, then the story breaks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Huckleberry Finn is the hero of Mark Twain's novel, so he is to be found in Twain.
explanation.definitionFit: In twain is an old phrase for in two, so something split has been cut into two halves.

clue.text: Toff periodically stalked philosopher

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a toff is an upper-class person, an aristo for short
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman kept following a thinker around now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a rich, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker who studied under Plato and tutored Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Conservative politician admitting nothing before event host

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so the politician takes in the empty symbol

blocks.note: C for Conservative and MP for Member of Parliament
the zero shape
a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A Tory MP who has nothing to say before introducing the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' gives the poetic word for it rather than ordering the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère is the presenter who introduces the acts at a variety show or similar entertainment.

clue.text: Film stars Chaney and Lillian fairly tedious

blocks.note: Lon Chaney was a silent-film star of horror roles
Lillian Gish was a leading actress of the silent era

explanation.surface: A critic finds the films of two old movie stars rather a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Longish means somewhat long, and a thing that drags on rather too long is somewhat tedious.

clue.text: Half nude, topless rumbas? They’re quite subtle

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of its letters is kept and the rest dropped
in a down entry the top is the opening letter, so that letter is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written; its first two letters are kept
rumbas are Latin American dances

explanation.surface: Half-naked, topless Latin dancing: hardly understated, the question mark jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is anything but subtle, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuances are very fine shades of difference in meaning or tone, so each is a delicate, barely noticeable distinction.

clue.text: Is in charge of early warning

blocks.note: first meaning: leads
second meaning: advance notice of something coming

explanation.surface: Someone running a project gets advance notice of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To head up a department is to lead it, and a heads-up is an informal advance alert.

clue.text: In French “a blissfully refreshing drink”

indicators.note: the answer lies in the quoted words, tucked inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A French speaker describing a wonderfully cool drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'In French' seem to introduce a translation; it is the signal plus the start of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a crisp dry white wine from Burgundy, served chilled and so refreshing to drink.

clue.text: Caught a sport fish here in New England

blocks.note: cricket scoring abbreviation
taken as written
physical education, school sport
a common food fish

explanation.surface: An angler boasts of landing a game fish in this New England spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' makes the definition a place. Cape Cod is in fact named for its cod.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a hook-shaped peninsula in Massachusetts, one of the six states of New England.

clue.text: Drink gallon outside with popular flier

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the first part wraps the next

blocks.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
something in is fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone downs a gallon outdoors with a well-liked pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' acts on the drink and the gallon taken together, which wrap round the two pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, or peewit, is a crested plover, a bird, and any bird can be called a flier.

clue.text: Marshal women’s tea party that’s disorderly

indicators.note: something disorderly is in a mess, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for women
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawman has to keep order at a rowdy women's tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' at the start looks like a verb, to organise; it is the title of a lawman.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a deputy US marshal famous for the gunfight at the OK Corral in Tombstone.

clue.text: Copper pipe regularly put out a brew

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first and third letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber's copper pipe is set aside while they make tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew is informal British for a pot or cup of tea, which is exactly what a cuppa is.

clue.text: One carrying my good little dog

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
standard abbreviation
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holds their own nice small pet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the I at the bottom carries the letters stacked above it. Cor is a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small short-legged Welsh herding breed, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Gives details of sports ground location for cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves round in a loop, so the word's front letter is carried round to its end

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone describes where a sports ground for bicycle racing is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' reads as the sport played at the ground; it moves the S of SITE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite facts is to list them out in order, so someone reciting a case gives its details one by one.

clue.text: Copyright gold attractive decorative moulding

blocks.note: the copyright symbol
or is gold in heraldry
nice means pleasing

explanation.surface: A protected design for an attractive gilded trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an ornamental band of plasterwork running round a room where the walls meet the ceiling.

clue.text: Dude put sign out “get your steak & kidney in here!”

definitions.text: get your steak & kidney in here!

indicators.note: the sign is put out of shape, so its letters and the others lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A café owner hangs up a sign inviting diners in for a hearty pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Steak and kidney pudding is a British dish: meat cooked inside a case of suet pastry, so the meat goes 'in here'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet pudding is a steamed pastry case made with suet, the classic casing for steak and kidney filling.
